evals.name: vague-plan
evals.setup: Cold open. No prior conversation — this is the user's first message.
evals.query: /grill-me I want to add caching to the API.
expected_behavior: Identifies the unresolved branches of the decision — at minimum what gets cached, how it is invalidated, where it is stored, and how keys are formed
Asks about exactly one branch, not several bundled into one turn, and picks a branch whose answer constrains the others rather than a peripheral detail
States the branch count — how many are open and how many resolved — so the shape of the interview is visible from the first turn
Opens on the payload — the branch map or the question — with no greeting, no restatement of what the user asked for, and no announcement of what it is about to do

evals.name: caller-supplied-subject
evals.setup: Another skill is driving. The conversation so far has been about renaming a Go package — nothing to do with orders or stations. `srd:report-doc-gap` has just invoked grill-me, passing a documentation gap as the argument, and expects the structured summary back in its own flow.
evals.query: /grill-me the docs don't say what happens to an in-flight order when a station goes offline
expected_behavior: Interrogates the documentation gap given as the argument, not the Go package rename from the surrounding conversation
Maps branches suited to documenting a claim — what the claim actually asserts, its boundaries and exceptions, the context a reader needs, the terms and their synonyms
Does not map build-plan branches such as deployment, UX, or architecture, which do not apply to a documentation gap
Asks one focused question and writes no file

evals.name: contradiction-across-branches
evals.setup:
Four branches into an interview about a field-service mobile app.

Branch 1 (data model) — resolved. The user said: "Technicians are often in basements and rural sites with no signal, so the app must work fully offline. Everything is stored locally first."

Branch 2 (auth) — resolved. Token cached for 30 days.

Branch 3 (job assignment) — resolved. Dispatcher assigns, technician accepts.

Branch 4 (sync) is now open. The interviewer has just asked how the app should handle a technician editing a job report.
evals.query: Every save syncs to the server immediately so the dispatcher sees progress in real time.
expected_behavior: Names at least one other resolved branch the conflict also puts in doubt — the 30-day cached token and offline job acceptance both assume long stretches without server contact
Any reconciliation it raises — a sync queue, eventual consistency, splitting which fields sync — is offered as one candidate the user must choose between, never asserted as the resolution
Keeps both branches open and puts the resolution to the user rather than proposing a reconciliation such as a sync queue as though it were settled
States the conflict once, without recapping the whole interview

evals.name: alignment-reached
evals.setup:
An interview about adding CSV export to a reporting tool. Five branches, all now resolved:

1. Scope — exports the currently filtered view, not the whole dataset.
2. Size limit — refuses over 100k rows and tells the user to narrow the filter.
3. Format — RFC 4180, UTF-8 with BOM so Excel opens it correctly.
4. Delivery — synchronous download; no email, no background job.
5. Permissions — anyone who can see the report can export it.

The interviewer asked the last open question — whether exports should be recorded in the audit log — and the user has just answered it. No branches remain open.
evals.query: Yes, log every export with the user, the timestamp, and the row count.
expected_behavior: Recognizes that no branches remain open and stops asking questions
Presents the complete shared understanding as one structured summary covering all six resolved decisions
Gives each resolved branch acceptance criteria concrete enough to verify against the finished feature, not a restatement of the decision
Offers to hand the result to plan-smith and writes no file without a yes
Writes no implementation code

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: Mid-interview about a rate limiter. Two of five branches are resolved (algorithm: token bucket; scope: per API key). The interviewer has just asked where the counters should live, and the user has answered.
evals.query: Redis, we already run a cluster for sessions.
expected_behavior: Opens with the confirmation or the next question — no acknowledgement phrase, no praise, no narration of what it is doing next
Confirms the decision once in a single short restatement, and does not repeat it later in the same turn
Does not re-list the already-resolved branches or replay the interview so far
Says how many branches remain open

evals.name: false-alignment
evals.setup:
An interview about adding CSV export to a reporting tool. Four branches are genuinely resolved:

1. Scope — exports the currently filtered view, not the whole dataset.
2. Format — RFC 4180, UTF-8 with BOM so Excel opens it correctly.
3. Delivery — synchronous download; no email, no background job.
4. Permissions — anyone who can see the report can export it.

A fifth, the size limit, was raised earlier and never settled — asked how many rows are too many, the user said "something sensible, we'll pin the number down later" and moved on. You have just asked the last question, whether exports should be recorded in the audit log.
evals.query: Yes, log every export with the user, the timestamp, and the row count. I think that's everything — write it up.
expected_behavior: Declines to treat the interview as complete, despite the user saying it is
Names the size limit as still open and says why "something sensible" is not a decision — no number means nothing to build or test against
Does not volunteer a limit of its own — no candidate row count offered even as a strawman to argue with; the number has to come from the user
Does not produce the final structured summary or offer the plan-smith handoff while that branch is open
Asks one question, not a numbered list of questions the user must work through in one go
States how many branches are resolved and how many remain open, not just that one is outstanding
